text:
BMAC gets $15,000 grant for backpack program
Published 2:00 pm Wednesday, November 19, 2025
WALLA WALLA — Blue Mountain Action Council in Walla Walla announced it received a significant boost to its Backpack Bridge Program in the form of a $15,000 grant from the Wildhorse Foundation.
The money will go to support the council’s weekend meal program that ensures elementary students who rely on free or reduced-price school meals do not go hungry over the weekend.
Backpack Bridge, started in 2017, provides participating students with a Friday meal kit containing two breakfasts, two snacks, two fruits, and two entrées — enough to bridge the gap until school meals resume on Monday.
Demand for the program has surged in recent years, nearly tripling in some schools. Last year, BMAC distributed more than 18,000 weekend meal bags, up from 11,000 the previous year.
“This support from the Wildhorse Foundation ensures that local children have consistent access to nutritious food, even when school is not in session,” BMAC CEO Danielle Garbe Reser said in the announcement. “When kids return to school on Monday nourished and ready to learn, the whole community benefits.”
The Wildhorse Foundation has awarded more than $19 million in grant funding since its establishment in 2001. For more information, visit the foundation’s website at thewildhorsefoundation.com.
